messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but they provide sample mean, standard deviation, sample size, and population mean. They likely want the standard error or something? But the tool calculates p-value. We can use the function to compute p-value. But the question: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". That might refer to the standard error of the sampling distribution under H0: sqrt(sigma^2/n). But we don't know sigma; we have sample std dev as estimate. So standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute that: sqrt(40)=6.3249, so 1.4/6.3249=0.2215 approx.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under H0: sigma/sqrt(n). Since we only have sample std dev, we approximate using sample std dev. So answer ~0.2215.

We could also compute p-value using the function. But the request didn't ask for p-value. It asked for standard deviation. So we should respond with the calculation. Provide explanation. Probably no need to call function. But we can mention that if we had population std dev, we'd use that. But we only have sample std dev. So we approximate.

Thus answer: about 0.2215.
